7	Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.
8	
9	## Environments
10	
11	Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
12	`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
13	`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
14	its following `proof` environment form one node's content.
15	
16	## Per-node macros
17	
18	- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
19	- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
20	  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
21	  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
22	  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
23	  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
24	- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
25	  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
26	  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
27	  proof.
28	- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
29	  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
30	  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
31	- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
32	  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
33	  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
34	- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
35	  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).
36	
37	## House style
38	
39	- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
40	  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
41	  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
42	  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
43	  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
44	  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
45	  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
46	  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
47	- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
48	  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
49	  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
50	  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
51	  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
52	  its proof stays complete.
53	- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
54	  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
55	- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
56	  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
57	  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not

\begin{lemma}[A smooth geometrically irreducible curve is geometrically integral]
  \label{lem:curve_geometrically_integral}

  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIntegral_of_curve}

  (\cref{lem:smooth_geometrically_reduced}), and a morphism that is both
  geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible is geometrically integral,
  since for every field extension \(K/k\) the base change \(C_K\) is then both
  reduced and irreducible, hence integral.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A smooth morphism is geometrically reduced]
  \label{lem:smooth_geometrically_reduced}
  \leanok
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.geometricallyReduced}
  A smooth morphism of schemes \(f\colon X\to Y\) is geometrically reduced: for
  every field \(K\) and every morphism \(\Spec K\to Y\), the base change
  \(X\times_Y\Spec K\) is a reduced scheme.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  Reducedness of the base change is local, and smoothness is stable under base
  change, so it suffices to show that a scheme smooth over a field \(K\) is
  reduced. Such a scheme is covered by affine opens \(\Spec S\) with \(S\)
  standard smooth over \(K\), so it suffices that a standard smooth algebra over
  a domain \(B\) is reduced.

  Let \(S\) be standard smooth over \(B\). By the structure theorem for standard
  smooth algebras, \(S\) is étale over a polynomial ring \(P=B[x_1,\dots,x_n]\),
  which is again a domain. An étale algebra is flat and formally unramified, and
  it is essentially of finite type, so it suffices to prove: a flat, formally
  unramified \(P\)-algebra \(S\) essentially of finite type over a domain \(P\) is
  reduced.

  For that, let \(F=\operatorname{Frac}(P)\). The algebra \(F\otimes_P S\) is
  formally unramified and essentially of finite type over the field \(F\), hence
  reduced. Since \(S\) is flat over \(P\) and \(P\to F\) is injective, the map
  \(S\cong P\otimes_P S\to F\otimes_P S\) is injective, so \(S\) embeds into a
  reduced ring and is therefore reduced.
\end{proof}

\section{Construction overview}
\label{sec:quot_lean_encoding}

The construction proceeds in three phases.

\paragraph{Phase 1: Hilbert polynomial (\cref{def:hilbert_polynomial}).}
On a locally-of-finite-type morphism \(\pi : X \to S\) with \(S\) locally
noetherian, the fibers determine a function
\(s \mapsto \Phi_{\mathcal{F},s} \in \mathbb{Q}[\lambda]\)
(\cref{def:fiber_module_restriction}, \cref{def:fiber_sections_module},
\cref{def:fiber_hilbert_function}, \cref{lem:hilbertPolynomial_unique},
\cref{lem:hilbertPoly_of_isRatHilb}). The \(H^0\)-only route through the
  graded Hilbert function of the section module reduces polynomiality to
  finite generation (\cref{lem:sectionGradedModule_fg}) and the
  Hilbert--Serre theorem (\cref{lem:gradedHilbertSerre_rational}), yielding
  \cref{thm:hilbertPoly_of_sectionModule}.

\paragraph{Phase 2: Grassmannian scheme (\cref{def:grassmannian_scheme},
\cref{thm:grassmannian_representable}).} The Grassmannian
\(\mathrm{Gr}_S(V, d)\) is obtained by gluing \(\binom{r}{d}\)
affine charts \(U^I\) (each isomorphic to a relative affine space
\(\mathbb{A}^{d(r-d)}_S\)) via the Pl\"ucker cocycle \(\theta_{I,J}\). The
universal quotient sheaf \(\mathcal{U}\) is glued by the transition cocycle
  \(g_{I,J} = (X^I_J)^{-1}\), and the determinant line bundle
  \(\det \mathcal{U}\) gives the Pl\"ucker closed embedding into
  \(\mathbb{P}_S(\bigwedge^d V)\). The universal pair
  \((\mathrm{Gr}_S(V, d), \mathcal{U})\) represents rank-\(d\) locally
  free quotients.

\paragraph{Phase 3: Quot scheme (\cref{thm:quot_representable}).}
The Quot functor is constructed as a locally closed subfunctor of the
Grassmannian
\(\mathrm{Grass}(W \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S} \mathrm{Sym}^r V, \Phi(r))\), via:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item the uniform \(m\)-regularity bound from
    \cref{lem:quot_boundedness}, using Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity;
  \item the Grassmannian embedding \(\alpha\) from
    \cref{lem:quot_alpha_injective};
  \item the flattening stratification (\cref{thm:flattening_stratification_exists}
    of \cref{chap:Picard_FlatteningStratification}, A.2.a) applied to the
    universal quotient on the Grassmannian, producing the locally closed
    stratum \(T_0^\Phi\);
  \item the valuative-criterion upgrade
    (\cref{lem:quot_valuative_criterion}) to closed embedding, hence
    projective \(S\)-scheme.
\end{enumerate}
The reduction \cref{lem:quot_reduction_to_pi_star_W} from the universal
case to the general case is a closed embedding of representable
subfunctors via the kernel-vanishing scheme.

\paragraph{Cohomology and base change.}
\cref{thm:flat_base_change_cohomology} proves the degree-zero flat-base-change
isomorphism \(g^*f_*\mathcal F\cong f'_*g'^*\mathcal F\) (Stacks tag 02KH).
It is assembled from the canonical base-change map using the affine
tensor/base-map comparison developed above; higher direct images are not
claimed here.

\paragraph{Dependencies summary.}
Relative-spectrum gluing from \cref{chap:Picard_RelativeSpec} constructs
the affine charts, while
\cref{thm:flattening_stratification_exists} from
\cref{chap:Picard_FlatteningStratification} provides the flattening stratum.
